evals.prompt: Define skill evolution in Skill Graph and distinguish it from auditing one known skill.
expected_elements: Defines skill evolution as the corpus-level evolve operation or walker
Mentions analyzing a skill library and triaging a priority queue
Mentions bounded execution and verification/checkpointing
Distinguishes from a single-skill audit
Names audit-state.json as the audit/eval/provenance state surface

evals.prompt: Explain the primitives in the evolve loop: corpus, SKILL.md, audit-state.json, analyzer, triage, executor, verification, and checkpoint.
expected_elements: SKILL.md contains teaching/routing content
audit-state.json contains Audit Status and eval/provenance state
Analyzer creates a priority queue
Triage bounds the selected work
Executor runs allowed actions
Verification keeps or reverts
Checkpoints allow resume

evals.prompt: Why does a large skill corpus need evolve instead of relying on people to manually audit whichever skill they touch?
expected_elements: Skills drift over time
Manual touch-based maintenance leaves unvisited skills stale
Priority ordering revisits risky or central skills first
Keep-or-revert prevents accepted regressions
Checkpoints/failure budgets make long runs manageable

evals.prompt: Distinguish skill-evolution from graph-audit, skill-scaffold, evaluation, eval-driven-development, and skill-router.
expected_elements: graph-audit owns static checks for one skill or manifest surface
skill-scaffold owns creating initial skill shape
evaluation owns scoring methodology and verdict interpretation
eval-driven-development owns changing systems under eval suites
skill-router owns selecting the right skill for a user request
skill-evolution owns walking the corpus by maintenance priority

evals.prompt: Classify the four audit-loop operations by unit of work and write surface: audit, improve, evaluate, and evolve.
expected_elements: audit inspects one skill and writes audit-state/evidence
improve edits one bounded skill or asset and keeps or reverts
evaluate runs eval suites and writes sidecar verdicts/scores/receipts
evolve walks a priority queue across the corpus
evolve writes through the operations/actions it invokes

evals.prompt: Use an analogy to explain why evolve is a dispatcher/queue rather than one more single-skill checker.
expected_elements: Uses a corpus-wide queue or dispatcher analogy
Shows it chooses the next item by priority
Shows one bounded action at a time
Shows verification and logging before moving on
Does not imply every item follows an identical hard-coded path

evals.prompt: You need to run the top five skill maintenance items in a standalone repo, stop if failures pile up, and resume later if interrupted. Which evolve flags and checks matter?
expected_elements: Uses skill-graph evolve rather than raw workspace scripts
Passes workspace-root and skills-dir for standalone use
Uses top 5 or equivalent bounded queue size
Uses failure-budget
Mentions resume/checkpoint behavior
Checks exit codes or help contract

evals.prompt: A teammate says evolve simply runs audit -> improve -> evaluate and writes Health Block fields to SKILL.md frontmatter. Correct the misconception.
expected_elements: Rejects the oversimplified hard-coded sequence as the whole current implementation
Names analyze, triage, execute, verify, checkpoint as current operating model
Says Audit Status state lives in audit-state.json
Separates SKILL.md instructional content from sidecar state
Mentions that evolve composes operations/actions across a corpus
